The same thing happens for us Yidden every year during Chodesh Elul. We want to make sure that everyone will be ready for Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur! So, we blow the shofar to let everyone know that it is time to get ready, just like the conductor blows his whistle.

We blow every day, again and again, giving us all many reminders to prepare to crown Hashem as king. Then comes Rosh Hashana. The train starts leaving the station. But even then, the “train” moves slowly. After Rosh Hashana, we still have a chance to do teshuva until Yom Kippur. And even after Yom Kippur, there's still another chance through rejoicing and dancing on Sukkos, Shmini Atzeres, & Simchas Torah!

We want to make sure that every Yid is written and sealed for a good, sweet new year!

Did you know that Chodesh Elul is kind of like a train departing from the station?

When it gets ready to leave for a long trip, the conductor wants to make sure that all of the passengers get on in time and nobody is left behind. So, with the help of his whistle, he lets everyone know that the train is preparing to leave.

the conductor blows his whistle. Hopefully, passengers will hear it and will be sure to board the train quickly. Every few minutes, the conductor whistles again. He whistles and whistles, giving everyone a chance to get on so they won’t miss the train.

Chodesh Elul is a special time. All over the world, Yidden spend this month preparing to crown Hashem as

King on Rosh Hashana. And as Lubavitcher chassidim,

The Tzemach Tzedek once said that if we knew how powerful the pesukim of Tehillim are, we would never stop saying them!

During the 40 days of Elul and Aseres Yemei Teshuva, we add extra Tehillim so that we finish the whole sefer. Every day, we say three kapitelach after shacharis. (By the time we reach Yom Kippur, we are left with 36 kapitelach which we say throughout that holy Yom Tov.) If you miss a day, first skip ahead to the kapitelach of the current day, and only then go back to say the ones that you missed.

We hear the shofar every day of Chodesh Elul, besides for Shabbos and Erev Rosh Hashana.

The first day of Rosh Chodesh (Lammed Menachem Av) is just for practice. After that, from Alef Elul and on, shofar is blown each day after saying the three special kapitelach.

Many other Yidden blow just four blasts during Chodesh Elul. Minhag Chabad is to blow a full set of ten blasts. Here’s how it’s done: First—Teki’ah, Shevarim, Teru’ah, Teki’ah. Next—Teki’ah, Shevarim, Teki’ah. Then—Teki’ah, Teru’ah, Teki’ah. These ten blasts represent the ten kochos of our neshama. We want our whole neshama to prepare for Rosh Hashana!

Further Reading: Hayom Yom 27 & 30 Menachem-Av, and 1 Elul; Likkutei Sichos vol. 2, p. 446;

Sefer Hasichos 5748 vol 2, p. 610; Toras Menachem vol. 77, pp. 175-177.

“לְדָוִד ה' אֹורִי” is the 27th kapitel of Tehillim. This kapitel is connected to Elul because it speaks about how Hashem is important and dear to us like the light of our lives. It also has hints to the Yomim Tovim of Rosh Hashana, Yom Kippur, and Sukkos hidden within it. We say this special kapital during shacharis (as part of Shir Shel Yom, before Ein Kelokeinu) and mincha (before Aleinu), starting from the first day of Rosh Chodesh Elul until Hoshana Rabba.

Since Elul is a time to check our behavior, it’s also a good time to check the things we use for mitzvos. Minhag Chabad is to have our tefillin and mezuzos checked in Elul. Doing so brings more brachos for the coming year.

When the Rebbe first announced that we should check them every year, some people were confused. Shulchan Aruch says that mezuzos need to be checked once every seven years!

The Rebbe explained: Sadly, there are people today who buy tefillin and mezuzos without being careful about what’s inside. Some might contain printed paper instead of handwritten parchment, and some might not have the right pesukim! And even if everything is good, ink nowadays doesn’t last so long. So, it’s very important to have our tefillin and mezuzos checked every year, and help others do the same. Ask your parents if they’ve done it yet, too!

Elul is a time to think. We make a Cheshbon Hanefesh, thinking about all the things that we did in the past year. We think about what we did well and about what we want to do better. This way, we can clean up our mistakes and come to Rosh Hashana freshly prepared to crown Hashem as our King!

Chodesh Elul is such a special time that we even have a special way to greet each other! We wish each other a “ּכְתִיבָה וַחַתִימָה טֹובָה לְׁשָנָה טֹובָה ּומְתּוקָה—that we should be written and sealed by Hashem for a good and sweet new year.” The Rebbe tells us that our brachos to each other during Elul are very powerful, and can help give everyone everything they need in the coming year.
